cleanIntro: The Obsidian45 is the .45-bore member of the Obsidian family and it is fully user-serviceable, but its baffle counts are its own: eight baffles in the main body and four in the ADAPT Module, not the counts printed in any other Obsidian book. Two Rugged statements govern the whole job. The tube, the ADAPT Module body, the front cap and the spring retainer are ALUMINIUM and are barred from an ultrasonic cleaner; and the rear mount is selected by what the host firearm's barrel does. The Obsidian45 is a suppressor, not a firearm — clearing the pistol it comes off is the pistol's own manual's job, not this one's.

steps.title: Clear the host pistol — read its own manual for how
steps.action: Magazine out, action open, then check the chamber by eye and by finger before the Obsidian45 is touched. Rugged puts this instruction at the head of the teardown because the can is still a bore extension until it is off the gun. Nothing in this book describes your particular pistol, so how it locks open, whether it locks open at all, and where its chamber can actually be seen are questions for the pistol's own operator's manual. Settle those first.
steps.prose: Large-bore pistol cans go on a wide spread of hosts, from 1911s to carbine uppers; no single clearing routine covers them.
steps.quote: WARNING! Before disassembling your Obsidian45™, first remove the magazine and check the chamber of the firearm to confirm that it is in a safe condition and completely unloaded. Failure to do so could result in serious personal injury or death.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Obsidian Disassembly, p.2
steps.warn: Magazine out and chamber verified before the can is handled.

steps.title: Never clean an Obsidian45 that is still on the gun
steps.action: The can comes off the host before any solvent, brush or tank comes near it. Rugged writes this as a death-risk warning, not a housekeeping note, because cleaning means gripping and twisting a tube that is screwed to a muzzle with a chamber inches behind your hands. Put the pistol down clear and open and treat the suppressor as a separate object on the bench.
steps.prose: Everything below assumes the can is already off the host. That is not an accident of ordering.
steps.quote: WARNING! Never attempt to clean a suppressor while it is attached to a host weapon, as this could lead to personal injury or death.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Service/Maintenance, p.1
steps.warn: Never clean an Obsidian45 while it is mounted.

steps.title: Obsidian45 mount choice — fixed mount or piston, decided by the host
steps.action: Look at which mount is fitted in the back of your Obsidian45 before you fit it to anything. Rugged assigns the two mounts by host action type: a fixed barrel firearm takes a fixed mount, and a Browning-action pistol — the tilting-barrel design most centrefire pistols use — takes the piston, so the can can float while the slide cycles. A fixed mount locked onto a tilting barrel stops the pistol working, because the barrel now cannot move.
steps.prose: The mount changes out through the spring retainer at the rear, so this is reversible; getting it wrong just means the gun will not run.
steps.caution: Fixed mount = fixed barrels only. Piston = Browning action pistols.
steps.quote: A fixed mount should be used on all fixed barrel firearms. The piston should be used on all Browning Action Pistols.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Thread Mount/Piston Installation, p.1

steps.title: Cool it down before it comes off
steps.action: Set the can down and let it reach a temperature you can hold, or put proper gloves on. A .45 can that has just run a magazine is hot enough through the aluminium tube to burn, and breaking a mount loose takes a firm grip rather than a fingertip one. Rugged's instruction is to allow the suppressor to cool before removal.
steps.prose: Rushing this drops a hot can on its front cap threads, which are the surfaces that index the whole stack.
steps.quote: WARNING! Never attempt to remove your Obsidian45 while the suppressor is hot without the proper protective gear. Allow the suppressor to cool before removal.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Obsidian Disassembly, p.2

steps.title: Spring retainer off the rear of the body
steps.action: Hold the main tube and back the spring retainer off counter-clockwise from the rear face. It is the collar behind the mount and it is what keeps the booster spring captive, so expect a little pressure to release as the last threads clear — unscrew it under control rather than letting it spring free. With it off, the mount and piston assembly are no longer trapped in the tube.
steps.prose: This is also the joint you open when you want to swap between the fixed mount and the piston.
steps.quote: Unscrew the spring retainer counter-clockwise from the main suppressor body.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Obsidian Disassembly, step 1, p.2

steps.title: Piston assembly out, then the front cap off with the piston
steps.action: Draw the piston assembly straight back out of the main body, then use that same piston as the wrench for the ADAPT Module's front cap, turning counter-clockwise. Rugged designed the piston to be the cap tool, so nothing else is needed; if the cap is carboned tight, an allen key dropped into the piston's slot gives the extra leverage without anything touching the cap itself. Keep the piston out of the cleaning tray until the cap is back on.
steps.prose: Pliers on that cap put jaw marks on the exact surface that has to seal and index against the last baffle.
steps.quote: Remove the piston assembly from the main suppressor body. 2. Remove the front cap from the ADAPT™ Module. You can use the piston as a tool to aid in removal. For additional leverage, an allen wrench may be inserted into the piston slot.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Obsidian Disassembly, steps 1–2, p.2

steps.title: ADAPT Module off the main body
steps.action: Hold the main suppressor body in one hand and rotate the ADAPT Module counter-clockwise until it separates. Grip the body and turn the module rather than the reverse, so the torque goes into the joint you mean to break instead of into the baffle stack sitting inside it. What you are left with is two tubes, each still holding its own stack.
steps.prose: This is a field operation as much as a strip one — it is how the Obsidian45 goes from long to short configuration.
steps.quote: With the muzzle cap removed, hold the suppressor body with one hand and rotate the Module counter-clockwise until removed.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — ADAPT Module Removal, step 2, p.2

steps.title: Push both baffle stacks out from the mount end
steps.action: Look in through the mount at the rear of the body and push the baffle cone forward with a finger or a wooden dowel rod until the stack walks out of the front. It always leaves forwards, the way the bullet went, because the baffles taper that way and the blast baffle is the biggest. The dowel is specified in wood on purpose — a steel rod on a baffle cone leaves a dent in the one face that has to sit square.
steps.prose: If the baffles are stuck to each other, the long end of a hex key in a baffle port prying against the inside of the baffle is the sanctioned way to break them apart. Lay them out in the order they come off.
steps.quote: Remove the baffle stack from the main suppressor body and ADAPT Module by pushing forward on the baffle cone from inside the mount with your finger or a wooden dowel rod. 5. Break the baffles apart one at a time. If the baffles are stuck together, a hex key can be used as a tool to aid in disassembly.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Obsidian Disassembly, steps 4–5, p.2

steps.title: No ultrasonic tank for the Obsidian45's aluminium parts
steps.action: Split the parts into two piles before anything gets wet. The tube, the ADAPT Module body, the front cap and the spring retainer are aluminium, and Rugged bars all four from an ultrasonic cleaner outright — cavitation plus a hot alkaline bath takes the finish off and then attacks the metal. Those four get a brush and a non-ammonia cleaner; only the steel goes in the tank.
steps.prose: It is the most expensive mistake this can offers, and you do not see it until the parts come out of the basket dull.
steps.quote: WARNING! The suppressor tube, ADAPT™ Module body, front cap and spring retainer are constructed of aluminum and should NOT be used in an ultrasonic cleaner to avoid damage.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Service/Maintenance, p.1
steps.warn: Tube, ADAPT Module body, front cap and spring retainer: NEVER in an ultrasonic cleaner.

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: In front of you should be the main tube, the ADAPT Module, the front cap, the spring retainer, the piston assembly and two separate baffle stacks. The Obsidian45's main stack is eight baffles — one blast, six standard and one short — and the module carries four more. Count them and keep the two stacks apart, because a module baffle in the main body is a bore mismatch you will not see once it is closed. Deep Clean covers the tank routine, the aluminium-safe route, and rebuilding both stacks in the right order and timing.
steps.prose: Note the counts are specific to the Obsidian45 and are not the same as any other Obsidian.
steps.quote: The main baffle stack consists of 8 baffles - 1 blast baffle, 6 standard baffles and 1 short baffle.
steps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Main Baffle Stack Assembly, p.2

deepSteps.title: Ultrasonic the steel only — piston, spring and baffles
deepSteps.action: The piston, the spring and the baffles go into an ultrasonic tank with a 50/50 mix of Purple Power and water for about an hour, then come out to dry. Rugged expects carbon to survive the cycle and says so plainly; that residue is cosmetic and does not need chasing. A wire wheel used to remove it will do more damage to a baffle cone than the carbon ever would.
deepSteps.prose: Dry them properly. Water trapped behind a baffle taper is how a stack seizes between range trips.
deepSteps.quote: Rugged Suppressors recommends cleaning of the piston, spring and baffles with an ultrasonic cleaner using a 50/50 mixture of Purple Power® and water. Allow the suppressor to be cleaned for approximately 1 hour, then remove the parts and allow to dry.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Obsidian Cleaning, p.1

deepSteps.title: The aluminium four get a brush and a non-ammonia cleaner
deepSteps.action: Tube, ADAPT Module body, front cap and spring retainer are cleaned by hand with a brush and a cleaner containing no ammonia. The specification is a chemistry, not a brand, because ammonia attacks aluminium and its finish directly. Concentrate on the internal threads and on the front cap's tool grooves — those are the surfaces that decide whether this can comes apart by hand next time or needs a wrench it should never see.
deepSteps.prose: Nylon bristles and patience beat a stronger chemical on this material.
deepSteps.quote: A non-ammonia based cleaner and brush can be used on the suppressor tube, ADAPT Module body, front cap and spring retainer in order to remove any carbon buildup.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Obsidian Cleaning, p.1

deepSteps.title: Build the main stack on the bench, short baffle first
deepSteps.action: Start the eight-baffle main stack on a flat, level surface with the short baffle cone-up, then build onto it. Each baffle indexes to the one below through machined tabs, so a stack assembled inside the tube cannot be checked and a stack assembled on a cluttered bench picks up a lean you will not see. Build the whole column first, then look down it.
deepSteps.prose: Squeeze the finished column and look for daylight between baffles before it goes anywhere near the body.
deepSteps.quote: Start by placing the short baffle on a flat, level surface with the cone facing up.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Main Baffle Stack Assembly, step 1, p.2

deepSteps.title: The blast baffle is engraved #1 and goes on last
deepSteps.action: The final baffle onto the main stack is the blast baffle, and Rugged identifies it for you: it carries a #1 engraved on its body. Read the engraving rather than judging by shape, because on a .45 stack the standard baffles look very alike at a glance. The #1 baffle is the one that takes the muzzle blast, so it belongs at the mount end of the assembled can.
deepSteps.prose: If there is any spacing between baffles once the stack is built, a rubber mallet seats them — never force.
deepSteps.quote: The last baffle will be the blast baffle. It is easily identified by a “#1” engraved on its body.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Main Baffle Stack Assembly, step 4, p.2

deepSteps.title: The ADAPT Module's own four-baffle stack
deepSteps.action: The module is not a hollow extension — it carries four baffles of its own, three standard and one short. Thread the empty module onto the main body first, then build its stack separately on the bench, short baffle cone-up, and keep it physically apart from the main stack. Twelve baffles live in a fully assembled long-configuration Obsidian45; count to twelve before you close it.
deepSteps.prose: The module's counts are not interchangeable with the main body's. Mixing them up is a bore mismatch, not a cosmetic error.
deepSteps.quote: The ADAPT Module baffle stack contains 4 baffles - 3 standard baffles and 1 short baffle.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — ADAPT Module Assembly, p.2

deepSteps.title: Time the module ports to the body ports
deepSteps.action: Insert the assembled module stack into the module housing and then rotate it so its baffle ports line up with the ports of the stack already sitting in the main body. Rugged calls port alignment a performance requirement, and this is the last moment it can be corrected before the front cap goes on. Sight down the bore and turn the stack until the port faces agree, then cap it.
deepSteps.prose: A can that got noticeably louder after a rebuild is usually a mistimed module rather than a worn baffle.
deepSteps.quote: Once the ADAPT Module baffle stack is fully assembled, it can be inserted into the ADAPT Module housing and then rotated to time the baffle ports in the ADAPT Module with the main suppressor body baffle stack ports.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — ADAPT Module Assembly, step 5, p.2

deepSteps.title: Let it cool before you change configuration
deepSteps.action: Swapping between the short and long configurations means unscrewing the ADAPT Module, and Rugged requires the body to be back at ambient temperature before you do it. Aluminium and steel at very different temperatures do not thread cleanly, and a hot module backed off a hot body is how threads gall. Wait for it, then change.
deepSteps.prose: This applies on the range, where the temptation to change configuration between strings is at its highest.
deepSteps.quote: When changing between the short and long configurations; make sure the suppressor body has cooled to ambient temperatures before attaching/detaching the ADAPT™ Module.
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — ADAPT Module Assembly, p.2
deepSteps.warn: Ambient temperature before attaching or detaching the module.

deepSteps.title: Grease the piston before it goes back on a booster gun
deepSteps.action: If your Obsidian45 runs the piston rather than the fixed mount, put white lithium grease on the outside of the piston at reassembly. The piston has to slide in its bore under recoil for the pistol to cycle, and a dry, freshly cleaned piston in a freshly cleaned bore is precisely when a booster stops stroking. It is the outside diameter that gets the grease.
deepSteps.prose: Do it every clean. Solvent takes the grease off as thoroughly as it takes the carbon off.
deepSteps.quote: When using a booster system, lubricate the outside of the piston with white lithium grease
deepSteps.cite: RUGGED SUPPRESSORS | OBSIDIAN45 | OPERATOR’S MANUAL — UNKNOWN — no revision or edition code is printed anywhere in the document — Obsidian Cleaning, p.1

cleaning.name: BAFFLES, PISTON & SPRING (steel — tank-safe)
tasks: Ultrasonic in a 50/50 mix of Purple Power and water, about one hour
Residual carbon after the cycle is acceptable and does not have to be removed
White lithium grease on the outside of the piston if you run a booster mount

cleaning.name: TUBE, ADAPT MODULE BODY, FRONT CAP & SPRING RETAINER (aluminium)
tasks: NEVER an ultrasonic cleaner — Rugged bars all four from the tank
Brush plus a non-ammonia cleaner to lift carbon buildup
Clear the internal threads and the front cap's tool grooves
Keep ammonia-based bore solvents away from these parts entirely

cleaning.name: MOUNT & HOST THREADS
tasks: Keep the barrel shoulder and mount face clean so the can seats square against a 90-degree shoulder
Confirm the fitted mount matches the host: fixed mount for fixed barrels, piston for Browning action pistols
Re-check the can is still tight on the barrel at 30 round intervals

reassembly: Build the eight-baffle main stack on a flat level surface: short baffle cone-up, six standard baffles, blast baffle #1 last.
Check for spacing between baffles and seat any gap with a rubber mallet, never by forcing the stack into the tube.
Insert the main stack into the main suppressor body with the #1 blast baffle cone facing down.
Thread the empty ADAPT Module onto the main body.
Build the module's four-baffle stack separately — short baffle cone-up, then the three standard baffles.
Insert the module stack and rotate it to time its ports to the main body stack's ports.
Thread the front cap on with the piston as the tool; an allen key in the piston slot gives extra leverage.
Fit the correct mount, refit the piston assembly, hand-tighten the spring retainer, and grease the piston OD if the host is a Browning action pistol.
fncheck: Sight through the bore against a light and confirm it is clear with no baffle edge intruding on the line. Confirm there is no space between baffles and that the front cap and spring retainer are hand tight without rattle. Check the fitted mount matches the host — fixed mount for a fixed barrel, piston for a Browning action pistol — and that the can seats firmly against a 90-degree barrel shoulder; if it tightens before it seats, or stays loose after it seats, stop and contact Rugged. Re-check that it is still threaded up at 30 round intervals while shooting.
